chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, from Wahb, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from Khalaf ibn Ḥammād, from the one who informed him, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man forgets to wipe his head while he is in salat (prayer). He said: “If there is moisture in his beard, then let him wipe with it.” I said: Then if he has no beard? He said: “He should wipe from his eyebrow or from the eyelashes of his eyes.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), during which the omission was remembered
key_terms.حَاجِبِهِ: his eyebrow, an alternative source of moisture
key_terms.رَأْسِهِ: his head, the place of obligatory wiping in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.لِحْيَتِهِ: his beard, from whose moisture wiping may be performed

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets to wipe his head in wudu (ablution) until he is already in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who forgets the wiping of the head during wudu (ablution) and only remembers while in salat (prayer). It explains that the required wiping may be completed using remaining moisture from the beard, or if there is no beard, from the eyebrows or eyelashes.
